newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Group cuts 23 executive staff.
newsitem.headline: Kia Group cuts 23 executive staff.

text.p: South Korea's struggling Kia Group said on Thursday it had cut 23 executives as part of its self-rescue efforts.
Kia said in a statement issued at a news conference the cuts were the first of a planned 30 percent reduction of executives.

The group also said the success of its recent discount car sale had enabled it to pay 36 billion won on Thursday to about 200 sub-contractors. It said it would pay 10.9 billion won to Pohang Iron and Steel Co in early August for raw materials.

The group also said Indonesia's Minister of Industries and Trade, Tunky Ariwibowo, had visited Kia Motors Corp's car plant south of Seoul and had been reassured that Indonesia's national car project would be unhindered by Kia's current troubles.
Kia Group chairman Kim Sun-hong and the Indonesian minister agreed to work together for successful completion of the project despite the current woes, the statement said.
